stations.about: Every retrograde of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto and Chiron from 2000 to 2040: station retrograde and station direct (UT, with degree and sign), and its length in days; typical, shortest and longest length.

ingresses.about: Every change of sign from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2030 for the Sun, Mercury to Pluto, Chiron and the true North Node (UT). retrograde: the body was moving backwards when it crossed, so it went back into the previous sign. The Moon changes sign every 2½ days and is left out.

conjunctions.about: Every exact conjunction (same ecliptic longitude, geocentric) from 1800 to 2100, UT; a retrograde loop can give three in one year.

longIngresses.about: The crossings in and out of a sign (UT), retrograde returns included.

generations.about: The signs of Uranus, Neptune, Pluto and Chiron at 12:00 UT on 1 January and 1 July of each year from 1930 to 2009.

lifeTransitsSummary.about: Across births on 1 January and 1 July of each year 1930–2009: the youngest and oldest age at the first exact hit of each life transit (births with no hit by the end of the computed span are counted apart). byYear: the ages for a birth on 1 January of every fifth year.

lifeTransits.about: For someone born at 12:00 UT on 1 January or 1 July of each year from 1930 to 2009: the ages (years, one decimal) at which the transiting body is exactly at that angle to its own birth position. Several ages in a row (a few months apart) are one passage with retrograde loops. Jupiter returns, nodal returns (transiting true node on the natal node) and nodal reversals (on the natal South Node) list one age per passage.

outOfBounds.about: Out of bounds: declination north or south of 23.44°, the Sun's greatest declination (the obliquity of the ecliptic), from 2026 to 2030, from AGS's ephemeris (astronomy-engine, apparent equatorial coordinates of date). The Moon: how many stretches each year and the highest declination reached; Mercury, Venus and Mars: each stretch.
